title: The Falling Calendar
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Trench keepers once dated years by the color of falling fragments; blue-white showers marked safe navigation seasons.

title: Stone That Remembers Heat
text: An old field report states: Fresh starstone remains warm for decades, and its inner light brightens when returned near its original crater.

title: A Bent Plumb Line
text: A local record preserves this account: A surveyor recorded that every weight leaned east here, although east changed whenever the largest fragment pulsed.

title: Crystalline Nursery
text: An unsigned observation reads: Tiny glass-finned fish shelter inside meteor cracks because larger predators cannot tolerate the harmonic ringing.

title: Do Not Lick the Comet
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: A handwritten addition reads: "It tastes like cold lightning. This warning exists because I made a scientific mistake. --Shizuki"

title: Annex Transit Mark
text: An old field report states: A faded cargo seal matches Moonlit Lab workmanship but bears a trench designation and a much later revision number.

title: The Quiet Impact
text: A local record preserves this account: One crater contains no debris, only a perfect absence where sound and current vanish at its rim.

title: Ventkeeper Record
text: An unsigned observation reads: Old divers harvested cosmic vent glass with copper tools; iron implements became too heavy to lift near the plume.

title: Borrowed Constellations
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Celestial fragments on the seabed form patterns absent from the sky, suggesting they fell from somewhere else.

title: Helpful Arrow Number Seven
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki drew seven arrows toward seven different tunnels and labeled all of them "probably the shortcut."

title: Deep-Orbit Shell
text: A local record preserves this account: A nautilus shell records a spiral matching the orbit of a star no modern chart recognizes.

title: Ruin Without a Sky
text: An unsigned observation reads: The oldest celestial arch was built before the surrounding impact, yet its carvings depict the fragment arriving.

title: Meteorwake Song
text: A damaged traveler journal records: When several shards resonate together, their notes reproduce a navigation hymn used by vanished trench settlements.

title: Gravity-Sick Journal
text: An old field report states: An explorer learned to sleep tied to the floor after waking on the ceiling three mornings in succession.

title: Emergency Mustache Protocol
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: A facility notice has been amended: "Facial disguise ineffective against security constructs. Still stylish. --S"

title: Buried Observation Lens
text: An unsigned observation reads: A cracked lens magnifies not distance but age, showing nearby ruins as they looked roughly a century ago.

title: The Star-Eater Trail
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Smooth grooves end at empty sockets where luminous fragments once rested, each surrounded by silver residue.

title: Unsent Cargo Complaint
text: An old field report states: An annex quartermaster objected to receiving sealed specimen crates without origin papers or living-content warnings.

title: Aurora Below
text: A local record preserves this account: Trench auroras rise from the seabed rather than descending from above and briefly reverse weak currents.

title: An Older Insignia
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: A corroded badge bears the organization mark beneath another emblem that someone deliberately filed away.

title: Cometglass Etiquette
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Local tradition held that taking the first shard from a new crater invited every falling stone to notice you.

title: The Weightless Camp
text: An old field report states: Bedrolls remain tied around a floating stone where travelers once waited for gravity to remember its direction.

title: Security Revision Forty-Two
text: A local record preserves this account: The annex repeatedly upgraded its pursuit protocols long after Moonlit Lab should have ceased operating.

title: Starwalker Footprints
text: An unsigned observation reads: A trail of fused footprints crosses molten-looking stone without approaching or leaving the site.

title: Return Visit
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki wrote over a warning placard: "I came back voluntarily, moved your furniture, and left voluntarily. Important distinction."

title: The Trench Map
text: An old field report states: A celestial map marks other facilities as dim points beyond the reef, but water damage erased their names.

title: Corekeeper Memorandum
text: A local record preserves this account: A maintenance order describes an artificial body expected to remain functional beyond the lifespan of its makers.

title: The Missing Shipment
text: An unsigned observation reads: Records mention "Subject Seven transfer materials," although the destination field has been cut from the page.

title: Annex Night Watch
text: A damaged traveler journal records: A guard log ends with reports of laughter in sealed ducts and every Officer portrait acquiring a paper mustache.

title: Not an Isolated Laboratory
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: The final surviving ledger confirms the Starfall Annex and Moonlit Lab reported to the same unseen authority.
